title: Route Fidelity Check
user: A cyclist or club ride leader who has a deliberate GPX route and needs to know whether a navigation app/device silently rerouted it before riders follow it.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A walking-club route creator says automatic completion reconnects waypoints on a nonsensical path and requests that only segments between deliberate waypoints be optimized.
A RideWithGPS route containing a rail trail becomes nearby roads after the Garmin handoff despite the trail being visible in Garmin's map.

recurrence: Two independent 2025–2026 route-authoring reports describe route mutation at the handoff layer. Severity is high for group rides because the leader may discover a bad route only while navigating.
current_workaround: Manually inspect the route in each app/device, add many shaping points, or discover the deviation after export.
incumbents_and_gap: RideWithGPS, Garmin Connect, Komoot, and Organic Maps plan routes, but each owns its routing engine. There is no neutral, tiny preflight that compares an intended GPX line with an exported/re-rendered line.
smallest_useful_product: Browser tool that accepts two GPX files, aligns them, highlights divergences over a user-set distance, and emits a printable cue/checklist. Non-goals: route planning, turn-by-turn navigation, accounts, or map-data editing.
success_measure: On a 30-pair corpus of planned and exported GPX files, the tool flags 90% of known material detours and produces a reviewable result in under 15 seconds.
monetization: free — it is a focused trust-building utility that can seed later paid club export packs if demand appears.
constraints: Process GPX locally; use permissively licensed base-map tiles only if a map preview is included; clearly distinguish geometric difference from a claim that a route is safe or legal.
why_distinct: It audits a route handoff instead of competing to be the next route planner.
